title: Per-tenant retention & legal-hold controls for scheduled customer exports
creator: Ravi Singh
description:
Problem: Customers have differing regulatory retention and data retention policies. Currently our scheduled CSV / S3 export pipeline applies a one-size lifecycle on exported objects which conflicts with tenant-level retention windows and legal hold requirements. This causes two issues: 1) customers with long retention or legal holds cannot guarantee exports won't be prematurely expired, and 2) customers with short retention requirements cannot force export objects to be deleted sooner than platform defaults.

Goal: Add per-tenant retention and legal-hold controls into the export orchestration so that each exported object (S3 CSV, manifest, snapshot) is tagged and stored with lifecycle and retention metadata derived from tenant config. Provide an administrative toggle for legal holds that prevents automated expiry until released. Ensure console UI and API expose settings, and maintain strong audit logs and KMS/HSM compatibility for encrypted exports.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Backend API to read/write per-tenant export retention policy (retention_days, min_retention_days, legal_hold_flag, legal_hold_reason)
- Export scheduler and delivery pipeline changes to stamp S3 objects with appropriate tags and apply object lock/legal-hold semantics where supported
- Manifest metadata includes retention_policy and legal_hold_id for downstream consumers
- Admin console endpoints and events for legal hold apply/release; audit log entries for all changes
- Migration tool to backfill retention metadata for pending scheduled exports in the queue
- E2E tests and integration test harness covering S3 object lifecycle tags, object lock behavior (mocked), and rollback semantics
- Documentation (confluence link) and runbook for Support and Success teams for handling legal-hold releases and disputes

Design notes:
- Prefer to use S3 Object Lock (governance mode) when customer's storage account supports it; otherwise rely on strong tagging + platform-enforced retention mower that avoids deletion until retention period elapses.
- Add an immutable legal_hold_id UUID stamped on manifests and objects; a legal_hold release must be an authenticated action with audit trail and approval comment.
- For exported artifacts stored in multi-tenant buckets, use object tags and our internal metadata manifest to decide lifecycle, do not alter bucket-level retention defaults except for objects that qualify for Object Lock.
- For Private deployments where KMS/HSM is customer-managed, ensure we are not taking ownership of SSE keys; document required permissions for object-lock operations.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Object Lock introduces complexity and cost (inability to delete objects may create storage pressure). We'll cap legal holds duration and introduce alerts for customers approaching quota limits.
- S3 Object Lock is not available on existing buckets without re-creation; for customers that cannot recreate buckets we will rely on tag-driven platform retention enforcement.
- Retention rules must be validated to prevent conflicts with export scheduling and retention_min limits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-tenant retention policy can be set via API and reflected in scheduled export runs
- S3 objects created by an export contain the retention_policy tag and legal_hold_id when set
- Objects under legal hold are not removed by platform retention sweeps and have audit entries for hold/apply/release
- Support runbook tested with simulated legal hold incident and clear rollback path
- Unit and integration tests added; CI green

Metrics / success signals:
- 0 production incidents of incorrect early deletion in first 30 days after rollout
- Reduction in customer support tickets related to export expirations for tenants with custom retention by 90%
- Telemetry: percentage of exports with non-default retention (target at least 25% for enterprise-tier customers)

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag backend API and metadata-only path (no Object Lock) to begin tagging manifests/objects; deploy to staging and canary
2) Enable platform retention enforcement for canary customers with agreed SLA
3) Gradually enable Object Lock path for customers with supported buckets and explicit opt-in
4) Enable console UI and legal-hold workflows; provide Support training and runbook

Security/privacy considerations:
- Any legal-hold release requires 2-step approval for customers marked "enterprise"; log the approver, timestamp, and free-text reason
- Ensure retention metadata is never used to bypass encryption requirements (SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS) and object lock usage respects KMS key policies
